summary: Amy Sims Miller works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied at Wesleyan University (BA, circa 1985–1989) and the University of Virginia (MA, circa 1994–2004), completing doctoral work under David Germano alongside traditional teachers.
Amy Snyder Ohta is a scholar in linguistics and Japanology. She studied at the University of California, Los Angeles in 1990 and held a post at the University of Washington around 1995.

Ana Agud is an Indology and linguistics scholar. She studied at the University of Salamanca (circa 1965–1974) and the University of Tübingen, later serving as Professor in Classical and Indo-European Philology at Salamanca (circa 1978–2018).

Anagarika Dharmapala worked in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Sri Jayawardenepura Maha Vidyalaya and Royal College, Colombo (circa 1878–1883), and founded the Maha Bodhi Society in 1891.

Anagarika Govinda worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a doctorate at the University of Freiburg, studied under Tomo Geshe Rinpoche, lectured at Patna University (circa 1935–1936), and served as Ācārya at Arya Maitreya Mandala (circa 1933–1985).
Anam Thubten Rinpoche is a scholar and teacher in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied under Tsurlo Rinpoche in 1979 and served as a teacher at the Vajrayana Foundation.

Ananda Coomaraswamy worked in Indology, history and archaeology, and philosophy. He studied at University College London (circa 1897–1900) and held posts at the Smithsonian Institution and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (circa 1917–1947).

Ananda W. P. Guruge worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Ceylon and University of London, later serving at NIEPA and as Dean Emeritus of Academic Affairs at the University of the West (circa 2000–2014).

Anant Sadashiv Altekar was a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University (circa 1930–1949), Patna University (circa 1949–1957), and served as Director of the Kashi Prasad Jayaswal Research Institute in 1955.

Anantalal Thakur worked in Indology and philosophy. He served as a professor at Mithila Research Institute (circa 1951–1969) and as Director of the Kashi Prasad Jayaswal Research Institute from 1968 to 1971.
Ananya Jahanara Kabir works in Indology. She studied at the University of Cambridge from 1993 to 1998 and took up a post at King's College London around 2013.

Andrea Acri works in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Leiden University (circa 2006–2011) under Arlo Griffiths and Willem van der Molen, joining École Pratique des Hautes Études in 2016 in tantric studies.

Andrea R. Jain is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at Southern Methodist University and Rice University before becoming Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Indiana University–Purdue University Indianapolis in 2010.

Andrea Schlosser is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. She completed a master's and doctoral studies at the Free University of Berlin between 2001 and 2014, supervised by Harry Falk and Ingo Strauch.

Andreas Doctor works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed a PhD at the University of Calgary under Leslie S. Kawamura (circa 1999–2003) and held a post at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute around 2003.
Andree Dominique Messent is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Bristol by 2003 under the supervision of Paul Williams.
Andrei Ivanovich Vostrikov was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy (Theodore Stcherbatsky) between 1920 and 1937.
Andrew B. Irvine specializes in philosophy and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Boston University by circa 2004 and became Assistant Professor of Philosophy at Maryville College around 2005.

Andrew Glass works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Bukkyo University and the University of Washington (1997–2006), where he completed his MA and doctoral studies under Richard Salomon.
Andrew Huxley was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at SOAS University of London in 1984 and subsequently held an academic post there from circa 1984 to 2011.
